methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Ideon Technologies is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Gary Agnew that has raised $30M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of nine private companies and one public peer (Lnza), all operating in the climate and energy sector at Series B through Series C stages. The private peer set includes KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, and Enovix.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $30M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical for Series B to next-stage step-ups, implying a valuation of $57M. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals at $3.0B (Series C), Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B (Series C), and Amogy at $700M (Series C). The median across this set is $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B.

Triangulating both methods yields a low estimate of $48M, a median of $528M, and a high of $1.1B. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty inherent in stage-progression methodology for early-stage companies and the inherent variance in peer valuations, particularly the stage differential between Ideon's Series B position and the Series C comparables used. Key uncertainties include the precise applicability of later-stage peer multiples and execution risk typical at the Series B stage.
